content: It outlines recommendations for monitoring, dose adjustments, contraindications, and alternative therapies based on the severity of interactions. 1. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases the metabolism of ethinyl estradiol. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is recommended. Consider using an additional non-hormonal contraceptive method for the remainder of the cycle. The mechanism is unclear but may involve CYP2C9 or CYP1A2 induction by ritonavir. 2. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases everolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and alternative drugs should be used. Close monitoring is essential if co-administration is unavoidable. 3. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases felodipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Therapy should be modified, and close monitoring is required. Consider reducing the felodipine dose by 50% during co-administration and for three days after the last dose of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir. 4. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases fentanyl levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring of fentanyl’s therapeutic and adverse effects, including potentially fatal respiratory depression, is recommended. Reduce the fentanyl dose if necessary. 5. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases finerenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of hyperkalemia, hypotension, and hyponatremia associated with finerenone. 6. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases flecainide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the potential for serious or life-threatening reactions. 7. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases flibanserin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of hypotension, syncope, and central nervous system depression. 8. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases fluticasone furoate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Co-administration may increase systemic corticosteroid concentrations, raising the risk of Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids such as beclomethasone or prednisolone. 9. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases inhaled fluticasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Similar to fluticasone furoate, caution is advised due to the risk of systemic corticosteroid-related adverse effects. 10. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases fosamprenavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients on ritonaviror cobicistat-containing HIV regimens should continue their treatment as indicated, with monitoring for adverse events. 11. Fosphenytoin decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated as it may lead to reduced nirmatrelvir plasma concentrations, risking loss of virologic response and resistance. 12. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases futibatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the potential for increased toxicity. 13. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases gepirone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases glecaprevir/pibrentasvir levels by inhibiting P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of increased serum concentrations and associated toxicities. 15. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases hydrocodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Close monitoring of therapeutic and adverse effects, including respiratory depression, is recommended. Reduce the hydrocodone dose if necessary. 16. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ibrutinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug due to the risk of severe adverse effects. 17. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases indinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Patients on ritonavir-containing HIV regimens should continue treatment as indicated. 18. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases irbesartan levels by weakly inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 19. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases isavuconazonium sulfate levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases itraconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the itraconazole dose to 200 mg/day during co-administration. 21. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ivabradine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of bradycardia or conduction disturbances. 22. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ivacaftor levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the dosage of ivacaftor or related combination therapies during co-administration. 23. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Limit the ketoconazole dose to 200 mg/day during co-administration. 24. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir decreases labetalol levels by inducing UGT2B7 metabolism. No dosage modification is needed due to the short duration of nirmatrelvir/ritonavir treatment. 25. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lenacapavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse reactions. 26. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases leniolisib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lidocaine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor therapeutic concentrations if available. 28. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lomitapide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of hepatotoxicity and gastrointestinal effects. 29. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases losartan levels by weakly inducing CYP2C9 metabolism. No dosage adjustment is required. 30. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases lovastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Discontinue lovastatin at least 12 hours before initiating nirmatrelvir/ritonavir and for five days after completing treatment. 31. Lumacaftor/ivacaftor decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 32. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases methylprednisolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for Cushing syndrome and adrenal suppression. Consider alternative corticosteroids. 33. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases midazolam levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Oral midazolam is contraindicated. 34. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases mirvetuximab soravtansine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for adverse reactions. 35. Mitotane decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 36. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases mometasone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for systemic corticosteroid-related adverse effects. 37. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases naloxegol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated due to the risk of opioid withdrawal symptoms. 38. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nelfinavir levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases neratinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 40. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nicardipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for side effects such as hypotension, flushing, and edema. 41. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nifedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the nifedipine dose by 50% during co-administration and for three days after the last dose. 42. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases nilotinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 43. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases norgestrel levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor for adverse effects. 44. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the dose to 50 mg/day and monitor closely. 45. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases oxycodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely for therapeutic and adverse effects, including respiratory depression. Reduce the dose if necessary. 46. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases palovarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47. Phenobarbital decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 48. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 49. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases pirfenidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 50. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases prednisone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely for systemic corticosteroid-related adverse effects. 51. Primidone decreases nirmatrelvir/ritonavir levels by inducing CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 52. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases propafenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 53. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. Reduce the quetiapine dose to one-sixth during co-administration. 54. Nirmatrelvir/ritonavir increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. This summary provides a detailed explanation of the interactions and recommendations for each drug.
